task_1.title: Restore generator-based field_transformer support
task_1.description: Version 25.3.0 restores a regression from 25.2.0 so class definitions using a generator-based `field_transformer` work again. The transformed attribute collection is now treated as a realized iterable before downstream validation, preserving expected behavior from 25.1.0.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to 25.3.0 restores support for `field_transformer` callables that return generators or other one-pass iterables, so attrs-based class creation behaves the same as it did before the 25.2.0 regression.

expectation.grounded: When a `field_transformer` is provided to attrs class-building APIs such as `@attr.s()` and it returns transformed attributes as a generator or other iterable, the library should fully realize that iterable before continuing attribute-order and class-construction processing. Generator-based `field_transformer`s that worked in 25.1.0 should succeed again in 25.3.0 without changing the public `field_transformer` API.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to supply `field_transformer` logic as a generator-producing callable and have class creation complete normally, with the yielded fields treated the same way as fields returned in a pre-built collection.

constraints.grounded: The fix must preserve existing behavior for non-generator `field_transformer` results while restoring compatibility for generator outputs. Attribute validation that runs after field transformation, including ordering checks based on the transformed field set, must still run against the final transformed attributes.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should broaden compatibility back to generator-style transformers without changing how already-supported transformers behave or weakening normal validation of the resulting fields.

behavior: A `field_transformer` may now return a generator and still participate successfully in attrs class creation.
Transformed attributes are consumed into a stable collection before later validation and construction steps run.
Post-transformation behavior continues to reflect the transformed field set, including any normal validation that depends on the final attribute ordering.
acceptance_criteria: When a class is declared with a `field_transformer` that yields its attributes from a generator, class creation should succeed instead of failing due to one-pass iteration.
When a `field_transformer` returns an already-materialized collection of attributes, the resulting class behavior should remain unchanged from prior supported releases.
When transformed fields violate normal attrs ordering rules, the library should still apply its usual validation after transformation rather than bypassing those checks.
